requirements_inventory.summary: Counter: POST /counter/increment adds one and returns the new value; GET /counter returns {"value": <n>}; a page has a button that increments and shows the value.

stack.summary: Proposed: Node.js (>=18) using only the built-in http module, no third-party dependencies, with in-memory state. The target directory is empty and neither the requirements nor the configuration name a stack; a zero-dependency Node server is the simplest common choice for two JSON endpoints and needs no install step.

milestones.title: Counter API
milestones.goal: Serve GET /counter and POST /counter/increment backed by an in-memory counter, and document both in openapi.json.

tasks.title: HTTP server skeleton
tasks.description: Create server.js using Node's built-in http module, listening on PORT env var (default 3000). Unknown routes return 404 with a JSON error body; wrong methods on known paths return 405. Add CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) and answer OPTIONS preflight with 204 so a separately served page can call the API.

tasks.title: GET /counter
tasks.description: Return 200 with Content-Type application/json and body {"value": n}, where n is the current in-memory counter value, starting at 0 when the server starts.

tasks.title: POST /counter/increment
tasks.description: Increment the in-memory counter by one and return 200 with Content-Type application/json and body {"value": n} holding the new value. No request body is required.

tasks.title: OpenAPI document and unit tests
tasks.description: Write openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.0) documenting only GET /counter and POST /counter/increment with the {value: integer} response schema. Add node:test unit tests that start the server on an ephemeral port and exercise both endpoints.

acceptance_criteria.text: On a freshly started server, GET /counter returns 200 with a JSON body exactly {"value": 0}.
POST /counter/increment returns 200 with JSON body {"value": n+1}, where n is the value GET /counter returned immediately before.
After three consecutive POST /counter/increment calls on a fresh server, the responses are {"value": 1}, {"value": 2}, {"value": 3} and a following GET /counter returns 200 with {"value": 3}.
GET /counter does not change the value: two consecutive GET /counter calls return the same {"value": n}.
GET /counter/increment returns 405 and GET /does-not-exist returns 404, and neither changes the value reported by GET /counter.

open_questions.question: Should the backend also serve the page with the increment button (e.g. GET / returning HTML), or is the page built by a separate frontend in the sibling workspace directory?
open_questions.context: COUNTER-1 mentions a page with a button. The target directory is named 'backend', suggesting a separate frontend. The plan currently excludes the page from the backend and enables CORS so a separately hosted page can call the API. If the backend should serve it, a milestone M02 adding GET / (200, text/html containing a button wired to POST /counter/increment and a display of the value) would be added.

assumptions.text: POST /counter/increment returns the new value in the same shape as GET /counter: {"value": <n>}, with status 200.
assumptions.source: COUNTER-1 says it 'returns the new value' without a shape; reusing the GET shape is the consistent reading.

assumptions.text: The counter starts at 0 and is held in memory; it resets when the server restarts. No persistence is required.
assumptions.source: COUNTER-1 names no initial value or persistence.

assumptions.text: The page with the button is out of scope for this backend loop (pending OQ1); the backend enables permissive CORS so a separate frontend can call it.
assumptions.source: Target directory is 'backend'; COUNTER-1 page requirement.

assumptions.text: The server listens on port 3000 by default (overridable via the PORT environment variable) and binds to all interfaces.
assumptions.source: Proposed; no port given in requirements or configuration.

assumptions.text: The counter is a single global counter with no authentication.
assumptions.source: COUNTER-1 describes one counter and mentions no users or auth.
